evidence: Plaut. Trin. 4.2.60; Ter. Eun. 2.3.77: cibum capere (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin has no general word for a meal apart from food: “have a meal” is cibum capere or cibum sūmere, “before the meal” ante cibum. The meals themselves have their names (see breakfast, lunch, dinner).

evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. cibus: syn. epulae
terms.comment: A rich or festive meal (see banquet).

phrases.latin: cibum tibi et familiae cūret utī coctum habeat
phrases.english: let her see to it that she has food cooked for you and the household
Wash your hands before the meal.

sources: Lewis & Short: cibus · Lewis & Short: epulae
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 72.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. meal.
